content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **StateFlow and SharedFlow** as part of **Coroutines, Asynchronous Programming, and Concurrency**. Flow represents an asynchronous stream collected from a coroutine; flow operators, cancellation, buffering, and sharing determine behavior. Use the subtopics—State-Holding Streams, Broadcasting Events, Replay, Buffering, and Subscriber Behavior—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: Asynchronous code introduces lifecycle, cancellation, and shared-state concerns. Structured concurrency and explicit data flow make these concerns easier to reason about.
